correctness.rationale: All-order proof: sensor optima are exactly k-edge matchings with two holes; every source admits 4k adjacent slides. For arbitrary targets, r missing N edges must be inserted. Each initially fully M-matched nontrivial symmetric-difference component (all alternating cycles and, if delta=1, one M-ended alternating path) requires an independent first nontarget disturbance, giving d>=r+c+delta. Explicit sequences eliminate cycles for q+1 slides each, mixed-hole paths for one slide per desired edge, and the delta=1 pair of exceptional paths with one temporary cross-path edge; hence equality. Cycle packing and explicit parity-based examples give exact diameter ceil(3k/2); S_n transitivity gives radius. Two standalone independent programs passed; full-graph BFS matches all-pairs formula for k=1..5, while independent graph forcing verifies all candidate optima up to k=4.

originality.rationale: The exact complete-graph nonbipartite TS lower bound, full all-pairs shortest-path formula with both alternating-cycle and two-hole-path surcharges, and sharp diameter were not found in inspected primary texts or closest publicly indexed results. A very close balanced complete-bipartite result already provides a specialized upper-bound route; this is acknowledged, not concealed. Its graph is a proper subgraph of the present complete graph and does not prove no nonbipartite shortcut. The new first-disturbance lower bound proves precisely that missing implication; a pairwise bipartite isometry and complete-graph diameter follow. The original power-domination criterion and state census are explicitly excluded from novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact-distance theorem for edge-token sliding on complete nonbipartite graphs may imply the new no-shortcut lower bound.
The complete-bipartite metric is very close and may permit a short reduction; priority depends on whether the extra unrestricted-shortcut lower bound was already established elsewhere.
The 2019 alternating-cycle-flip source was inspected at abstract/record level only; its distinct move rule is established, but complete paper priority was not asserted.

value.rationale: The natural optimum sensor relocation question demands the shortest sequence of physically adjacent moves. The all-pairs formula identifies an unbounded per-cycle surcharge and a separate two-hole path obstruction beyond target-edge differences, gives a constructive optimal route and exact global diameter, and shows pairs are isometric to suitable balanced bipartite subproblems despite extra nonbipartite edges. These extend the known optimum sensor census by a nontrivial complete-graph lower bound, rather than changing labels or recomputing a table.
